# Native text-shadow line metrics and painting

Original, manually authored OOXML; no template artwork or font binaries are
distributed. `tools/text_shadow_line_metrics_fixture.py` generates twelve
pages: Corbel 16 regular, Rockwell 36 bold italic, and Rockwell 66 bold, each
with plain text, shadow, outline, and both effects. Each page has three manual
lines followed by an unaffected Arial marker. The shadow is 3 pt at 44 degrees,
without blur, scaling, or skew. The outline is 1 pt. Mark and run properties
match. The 2010 WordprocessingML (w14) extensions are declared MCE-ignorable.

`native.pdf` was exported by the reference application using
`tools/export-reference.ps1`. Run
`python tools/text_shadow_line_metrics_reference.py` to regenerate the hashed
native baseline record. Outlined text becomes PDF paths, so its following
plain marker supplies an independent total-height measurement.

Run `node tools/check-text-shadow-line-metrics.mjs [output.json]` with Vite
running at port 5173 (override with DOCX_TEST_URL). Installed Corbel, Rockwell,
and Arial are required. The diagnostic compares native extracted text origins
within 0.15 pt; this accommodates PDF text-coordinate rounding, not the larger
missing effect. It exits nonzero on any native mismatch.

The initial diagnostic had twelve origin mismatches on its six shadow-bearing
pages. Relative to plain controls, the reference application moves
the following marker down 2.16, 3.84, and 5.88 pt across the three respective
font cases. The first shadowed baseline remains unchanged. Outline alone does
not change line height in these controls.

Seven additional original packages, generated by
`tools/text_shadow_matrix_fixture.py` from `cases.json`, establish the generic
layout behavior. Each package has its own independently exported native reference PDF:

- `matrix`: 21 pages covering cardinal directions, distance, blur, different
  letter shapes, whitespace, and run versus paragraph-mark effects.
- `sizes`: 42 pages, three font families and seven font sizes.
- `scale-check`: 12 independent checks of the nonlinear scale, including
  fractional sizes and sizes above 72 pt.
- `fraction-transform`: 24 pages covering whole/half-point pairs, scaling,
  reflection and skew.
- `skew-width`: 12 pages proving allocation is independent of string length.
- `skew-fonts`: 18 pages establishing the allocation width as twice font ascent.
- `defaults`: 15 pages covering transparent shadows, omitted attributes and
  all nine alignments with vertical scaling.

All 156 pages now match extracted native text origins within 0.15 pt. The reference application
scales effect distance/blur by `(floor(fontSize)/72)^0.7`, includes fully
transparent run effects in layout, and uses zero omitted scale factors.
The first two are empirical compatibility rules beyond the spec's attribute
descriptions; the last matches its stated default. See docs/conformance.md for
specification links and remaining verification boundaries. The declaration is
preserved; only computed geometry uses this scale.

`tools/text_shadow_paint_reference.py` samples independently rendered native
gray shadow interiors, excluding two display pixels around any hard edge.
`matrix-paint-reference.json` contains 128 samples across the four 12 pt
directional-shadow pages, with 24-level RGB tolerance. The smaller offsets have
no sufficiently wide interior at 96 dpi and are checked by layout measurements
and visual pairs, not empty pixel assertions. Browser tests repeat these samples
through editing, undo and export/reopen and separately check that mixed-run
shadows extend beyond their source formatting window without changing shaping.
As with the other native-font browser oracles, the native paint workflow is
explicitly skipped when Rockwell is unavailable. The portable mixed-run check
and model/import/export tests remain enabled. No proprietary fonts are bundled.

The 12 original plain/outline/shadow page pairs were visually inspected. The
paint sample oracle does not establish pixel identity or comprehensive native
paint conformance for blur, scale, skew, script scaling or decorative text.
Those remain explicit follow-ups. Exact/nonautomatic paragraph spacing and
empty paragraphs also need additional native controls.
